discovery: Invention and realization of the high-gain X-ray free-electron laser (SASE XFEL)

nominees.name: Claudio Pellegrini
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Kwang-Je Kim
nominees.affiliation: Argonne National Laboratory and University of Chicago, USA

nominees.name: Jörg Rossbach
nominees.affiliation: University of Hamburg and DESY, Germany

subfield: Accelerator physics / X-ray science (probes of condensed matter)
motivation: The X-ray free-electron laser is the most important new light source since the synchrotron. Pellegrini proposed using self-amplified spontaneous emission from a high-brightness electron beam to reach coherent Ångström-wavelength radiation, the idea behind LCLS. Kim developed the high-gain FEL theory, including the brightness and emittance criteria that made the scheme workable. Rossbach led the TESLA Test Facility and FLASH, which gave the first demonstration of SASE saturation at short wavelengths and opened the way to the European XFEL. The result is a source with a billion times the peak brilliance of synchrotrons and femtosecond pulses. It has changed how we see matter: we can now make molecular movies, image single particles, run time-resolved RIXS on quantum materials and watch charge order and electron dynamics on their natural timescales. This is a new way of seeing matter that grew out of fundamental physics.
